finding: A possibility-conditioned assembly preprocessor candidate can run before every material prompt and expose a bounded, counterevidence-preserving active assembly, reducing dependence on the model first deciding whether/how to retrieve. This is compatible with FRANK's ActiveAssembly direction but is not yet an H1 release mechanism or measured superiority result.
counterhypotheses: Always-on preprocessing may waste latency on easy prompts or overcompress rare decisive evidence.
A simpler typed retrieval policy may match downstream outcome at lower rebuild/context cost.
required_next_measurement: H1 matched traces: preprocessor-on-every-prompt vs model-triggered retrieval vs typed query plane vs raw/full-state baselines, with task outcome, omission/counterevidence, latency, token/KV cost and re-expansion metrics.
identity_boundary: Research Entity != Frank; candidate activation/rank cannot mint Frank execution authority.
target_scope: Final Frank v0.1 acceptance remains Andreas Ubuntu only.
